criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Three frames are strong. 04 (brass stack at macro, dark field, warm seam) and 07 (blued stack under a raised pan) are bold single subjects with true blacks, and 03 is a countable case: from the thumb I count 19 brass, 15 blued, 1 nickel and 4 empty wells. Four frames hold the score down. 02 is a flat grey sheet over the right two thirds, with a hard vertical seam against the pecan strip and a dead black band under the dek, and its single weight reads as a button. 05 is two thin rows of small discs across the lower half of a cracked clay board with the upper half empty, so it reads as a striped chart. 08 is a generic CG dais with a shut box: warm walnut mid tones under a flat navy wall, and nothing in the image shows 'draft'. 06 nearly repeats 01's camera. Its pans and stacks are cut by the bottom edge under the footer, and the mono label 'THE NEEDLE ON THE RESERVE' floats. The flow summary lists 06 as not repaired, 02 and 08 as strobes 'declared rather than delivered', and 04 and 07 knurl reading as bars.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: One balance runs through the deck, and the colour code holds on every frame that carries weights: brass is the chatbot and blued steel is the watcher, on 01, 03, 04, 05, 07 and 09. Casts fall lower right consistently (the 02 weight, the 03 wells). Motif evolution works, from loaded on 01 to stacked on 04, laid in rows on 05, the raised pan on 07 and back to loaded on 09. Two frames sit outside. 02 has grey paper and no colour code. 08 is a lit warm interior with the weights hidden in a shut case. The flow summary concedes the value arc 'strobes at 02 and 08'.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces. 190,000, 150,000, 10,000, 40,000 and 390,000 come from c1 to c4. 293,286 is c15. 49, 79, 133, 39/19/15/1/4 and 40,000 as the difference are all in figures.json with stated bases, and I rechecked 150/190 = 0.789, 190/390 = 0.487 and 390000/293286 = 1.33. Sources are primary: Legistar matter and event, the Census files, and Darwin's own site for Darwin's claims, which every surface attributes. 'Approved' is held to the draft minutes' word (slide 8, caption), and no surface says the council voted. One looser phrasing: the cover hook 'a watcher for it' ties Darwin's purpose to the chatbot, and no city record states that. The storyboard's own fact-check point 3 says 'Nothing says what Plano will use it for'. The item (f) letter rests on c6's note rather than its quote.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A reader learns what, where and how. Plano's City Council, on its October 12th agenda, put ChatGPT Enterprise plus a monitoring platform on the consent agenda, acted on in one motion, with a $390,000 ceiling and minutes still in draft. They do not learn what they can do. No next council meeting, no date for approving the minutes, no comment route, and no named decider beyond 'the council'. Collin and Denton counties appear only in the hashtags. The stake is general. The strongest resident-facing fact in claims.json, c12 (Darwin says it catches sensitive data in prompts and responses), is never used, so 'watcher' never says whose data or whose work it watches. The close, slide 9's 'about 133 cents a resident', makes the stake smaller rather than sharper, and its kicker 'Where it was decided' does not match its content.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover hook 'A chatbot for Plano, and a watcher for it' earns the swipe, and frame 2 (one motion, consent agenda) pays at once. Then three consecutive frames re-slice arithmetic that frame 3 already shows whole: 04 '49 percent', 05 '79 cents', 06 'The difference equals the reserve'. 06 is a numeric coincidence presented as a reveal, and its own dek says 'The tilt is a drawing', so it is cuttable. The printed kicker 'The turn' on 05 announces a turn instead of delivering one. The real turn, what the watcher does, comes on 07. The close lands on a per-resident division rather than a consequence or an action.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and house-rule compliant, and the caption opener '$390,000 is not what ChatGPT costs Plano.' is good. But 'Drawn to illustrate.' ends eight of nine deks as boilerplate, which is a machine tell in the feed. Several lines are flat or stilted: 'Each weight is $10,000, a drawing unit.' (01), 'Of the ceiling, 49 percent covers the chatbot' (04, inverted syntax), 'A ceiling of about 133 cents a resident' (09), where a Texan says $1.33. The storyboard planned '$1.33' and the shipped frame drifted. The caption carries a meta line, 'The deck weighs the item on a brass balance'. Plano is named, but nothing local beyond the name gives Texas texture.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The subject is fresh against the 30 day ledger: a city procurement read off Legistar, with no Plano or ChatGPT deck in the window. A balance as the spine and a chatbot against a watcher as the opening move are new. Familiar moves repeat from the last four to seven decks: the lastLight world (nos. 56, 57, 58, 60, 61, 62 per the topics ledger), brass as the hero metal (57's brass datum, 60's brass hex plugs), and drawing-unit counting reliefs (60 bores, 62 'drawing units of 10 MW', 56 bays).

one_sentence_fix: Cut frame 6's coincidence ('the difference equals the reserve') and spend that frame and the close on what a Plano resident can act on, which means fetching the next City Council meeting where the draft minutes come up for approval and its public comment route, and bring c12 forward (Darwin says it catches sensitive data in prompts and responses) so 'the watcher' has a concrete stake in residents' data instead of ending on 133 cents.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Generic CG dais with a shut box. Warm walnut fills the lower half in mid tones under a flat navy wall, and nothing in the image shows 'approved but still a draft', so the frame explains nothing at feed size.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Open the case on the ledge so the brass and blued weights show, lay an unbound minutes sheet beside it under the raking window key, and crop tight at ledge height so case and sheet own half the frame. Let the light fall off to black on the wall rather than lighting the navy.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Flat grey sheet over the right two thirds with a hard vertical seam against the pecan strip and a dead black band under the dek. The single weight reads as a button seen from above. It is the deck's one mid-grey frame.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Re-shoot the sheet as a low oblique txthree camera so the slotted weight stands as a tall brass cylinder casting a long shadow across the consent rows. Bleed the sheet off both sides to remove the seam, and pool the key on row (f) so the paper falls to dark.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Two thin rows of small discs across the lower half of a cracked clay board with the upper 45 percent empty, so the turn frame reads as a flat striped bar chart.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Drop the camera to a low oblique looking along the grooves so the discs stand as receding cylinders. Fill about 60 percent of the frame height, with the four empty blued wells lit in the foreground as the focal point.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Near repeat of 01's camera. Pans and stacks are cut by the bottom edge under the footer, the arc carries no visible graduations, and the floating mono label does the work the image should.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Build the planned macro with the pillar pushed off frame left and the camera level with the arc at 0.3 m, so the needle tip on its index and the engraved graduations fill the lower half. Otherwise cut the frame, as the one sentence fix proposes.
